pairs: Nunc autem derident me juniores tempore,
But now, those younger in years scorn me,
quorum non dignabar patres ponere cum canibus gregis mei:
whose fathers I would not have seen fit to place with the dogs of my flock,
quorum virtus manuum mihi erat pro nihilo,
the strength of whose hands was nothing to me,
et vita ipsa putabantur indigni:
and they were considered unworthy of life itself.
egestate et fame steriles,
They were barren from poverty and hunger;
qui rodebant in solitudine,
they gnawed in solitude,
squallentes calamitate et miseria.
layered with misfortune and misery.
Et mandebant herbas,
And they chewed grass
et arborum cortices,
and the bark from trees,
et radix juniperorum erat cibus eorum:
and the root of junipers was their food.
qui de convallibus ista rapientes,
They took these things from the steep valleys,
cum singula reperissent,
and when they discovered one of these things,
ad ea cum clamore currebant.
they rushed to the others with a cry.
In desertis habitabant torrentium,
They lived in the parched desert
et in cavernis terræ,
and in caves underground
vel super glaream:
or above the rocks.
qui inter hujuscemodi lætabantur,
They rejoiced among these kinds of things,
et esse sub sentibus delicias computabant:
and they considered it delightful to be under thorns.
filii stultorum et ignobilium,
These are the sons of foolish and base men,
et in terra penitus non parentes.
not even paying any attention to the land.
Nunc in eorum canticum versus sum,
Now I become their song,
et factus sum eis in proverbium.
and I have been made into their proverb.
Abominantur me,
They loathe me,
et longe fugiunt a me,
and so they flee far from me,
et faciem meam conspuere non verentur.
and they are not reluctant to spit in my face.
Pharetram enim suam aperuit,
For he has opened his quiver
et afflixit me,
and has afflicted me,
et frenum posuit in os meum.
and he has placed a bridle in my mouth.
Ad dexteram orientis calamitates meæ illico surrexerunt:
Immediately, upon rising, my calamities rise up to the right.
pedes meos subverterunt, et oppresserunt quasi fluctibus semitis suis.
They have overturned my feet and have pressed me down along their way like waves.
Dissipaverunt itinera mea;
They have diverted my journeys;
insidiati sunt mihi,
they have waited to ambush me,
et prævaluerunt:
and they have prevailed,
et non fuit qui ferret auxilium.
and there was no one who might bring help.
Quasi rupto muro,
They have rushed upon me,
et aperta janua,
as when a wall is broken
irruerunt super me,
or a gate opened,
et ad meas miserias devoluti sunt.
and they have been pulled down into my miseries.
Redactus sum in nihilum:
I have been reduced to nothing.
abstulisti quasi ventus desiderium meum,
You have taken away my desire like a wind,
et velut nubes pertransiit salus mea.
and my health has passed by like a cloud.
Nunc autem in memetipso marcescit anima mea,
But now my soul withers within myself,
et possident me dies afflictionis.
and the days of affliction take hold of me.
Nocte os meum perforatur doloribus,
At night, my bone is pierced with sorrows,
et qui me comedunt,
and those who feed on me,
non dormiunt.
do not sleep.
In multitudine eorum consumitur vestimentum meum,
By the sheer number of them my clothing is worn away,
et quasi capitio tunicæ succinxerunt me.
and they have closed in on me like the collar of my coat.
Comparatus sum luto,
I have been treated like dirt,
et assimilatus sum favillæ et cineri.
and I have been turned into embers and ashes.
Clamo ad te,
I cry to you,
et non exaudis me:
and you do not heed me.
sto,
I stand up,
et non respicis me.
and you do not look back at me.
Mutatus es mihi in crudelem,
You have changed me into hardness,
et in duritia manus tuæ adversaris mihi.
and, with the hardness of your hand, you oppose me.
Elevasti me,
You have lifted me up,
et quasi super ventum ponens;
and, placing me as if on the wind,
elisisti me valide.
you have thrown me down powerfully.
Scio quia morti trades me,
I know that you will hand me over to death,
ubi constituta est domus omni viventi.
where a home has been established for all the living.
Verumtamen non ad consumptionem eorum emittis manum tuam:
Truly, then, you do not extend your hand in order to consume them,
et si corruerint,
and if they fall down,
ipse salvabis.
you will save them.
Flebam quondam super eo qui afflictus erat,
Once, I wept over him who was afflicted,
et compatiebatur anima mea pauperi.
and my soul had compassion on the poor.
Expectabam bona,
I expected good things,
et venerunt mihi mala:
but evil things have come to me.
præstolabar lucem,
I stood ready for light,
et eruperunt tenebræ.
yet darkness burst forth.
Interiora mea efferbuerunt absque ulla requie:
My insides have seethed, without any rest,
prævenerunt me dies afflictionis.
for the days of affliction have prevented it.
Mœrens incedebam sine furore;
I went forth mourning, without anger,
consurgens,
and rising up,
in turba clamabam.
I cried out in confusion.
Frater fui draconum,
I was the brother of snakes,
et socius struthionum.
and the companion of ostriches.
Cutis mea denigrata est super me,
My skin has become blackened over me,
et ossa mea aruerunt præ caumate.
and my bones have dried up because of the heat.
Versa est in luctum cithara mea,
My harp has been turned into mourning,
et organum meum in vocem flentium.
and my pipes have been turned into a voice of weeping.
